layers.title: The Root
layers.subtitle: What this Name means linguistically
layers.content:
The Name Ar-Raqeeb (الرَّقِيب)

The Ever-Watchful

The Name comes from the root ra-qa-ba (ر ق ب), meaning to watch, to observe closely, to keep guard over. Ar-Raqeeb is the One whose watching never lapses — an observer who guards and preserves what He observes.

This Name is established for Allah in His Book and affirmed among the Most Beautiful Names, as the Prophet said: 'Verily to Allah belongs ninety-nine names, one hundred less one. Whoever enumerates them will enter paradise.' (Sahih Muslim)
layers.quran_ref: Quran 4:1 — 'Indeed Allah is ever, over you, Ar-Raqeeb (an Observer).'
layers.hadith_ref: The Prophet said: Verily to Allah belongs ninety-nine names, one hundred less one. Whoever enumerates them will enter paradise. — Sahih Muslim
layers.source: Sheikh Ibn Uthaymeen, Commentary on the 99 Names of Allah

layers.title: The Meaning
layers.subtitle: The full understanding of this Name
layers.content: The Ever-Watchful — the One who observes all things at all times, from whom nothing is hidden and nothing is absent. His watching is not the watching of suspicion but of complete knowledge and complete guardianship: He witnesses every deed, hears every word, and knows every intention concealed in the chest. He watches over His creation to preserve and protect it, and He watches over the deeds of His servants to recompense them with perfect justice. Because He is Ar-Raqeeb, the believer is never truly alone and never truly unseen — and this awareness is the root of ihsaan, worshipping Allah as though you see Him.
layers.quran_ref: Quran 4:1 — 'Indeed Allah is ever, over you, Ar-Raqeeb (an Observer).'
layers.source: Sheikh Ibn Uthaymeen, Commentary on the 99 Names of Allah

layers.title: In the Quran
layers.subtitle: Where Allah calls Himself by this Name
layers.content:
Allah calls Himself Ar-Raqeeb in the Quran. The placement of each Name is not accidental — when Allah closes a verse with a Name, He is signalling that the meaning of that Name is the reason for what preceded it.

Quran 4:1 — 'Indeed Allah is ever, over you, Ar-Raqeeb (an Observer).'

Related verses: 'And you, [O Allah], were the Observer over them.' (Quran 5:117) — 'And Allah is, over all things, an Observer.' (Quran 33:52) — 'Man does not utter any word except that with him is an observer prepared [to record].' (Quran 50:18)

The scholars of tafseer note that knowing which Name closes which verse deepens understanding of the Quran itself. The Name is the key to the verse.
layers.quran_ref: Quran 4:1 — 'Indeed Allah is ever, over you, Ar-Raqeeb (an Observer).'
layers.source: Sheikh Ibn Uthaymeen, Commentary on the 99 Names of Allah

layers.title: The Scholar
layers.subtitle: Ibn Uthaymeen's explanation
layers.content:
Sheikh Ibn Uthaymeen (rahimahullah), one of the foremost scholars of the 20th century, explained the Name Ar-Raqeeb:

The Ever-Watchful — the One who observes all things at all times, from whom nothing is hidden and nothing is absent. His watching is not the watching of suspicion but of complete knowledge and complete guardianship: He witnesses every deed, hears every word, and knows every intention concealed in the chest. He watches over His creation to preserve and protect it, and He watches over the deeds of His servants to recompense them with perfect justice. Because He is Ar-Raqeeb, the believer is never truly alone and never truly unseen — and this awareness is the root of ihsaan, worshipping Allah as though you see Him.

Ibn Uthaymeen taught that truly knowing the Names of Allah changes a person — not merely memorising them, but understanding their meaning and then living in light of them. He who knows Allah as Ar-Raqeeb will relate to Allah differently, supplicate to Him differently, and trust in Him differently.
layers.source: Sheikh Ibn Uthaymeen, Commentary on the 99 Names of Allah

layers.title: Your Reflection
layers.subtitle: What this Name means for your life
layers.content:
The Name Ar-Raqeeb is not only something to know about Allah — it is something to live in relation to.

The Prophet said: 'Verily to Allah belongs ninety-nine names. Whoever enumerates them will enter paradise.' The word for enumerate — ahsaha — means to know, understand, act upon, and call upon Allah by each Name appropriately.

Reflect: When do you most need to call upon Allah as Ar-Raqeeb? What situation in your life right now makes this particular Name the one you need most? The Names of Allah are not a list to memorise — they are doors to knock on in different moments of need.

The Quran says: 'And to Allah belong the best Names, so call upon Him by them.' (7:180)

quiz.prompt: What is the primary meaning of the Name Ar-Raqeeb?

options.text: The Ever-Watchful
The Ever-Forgiving
The Ever-Generous
The Ever-Patient

quiz.citation: Sheikh Ibn Uthaymeen, Commentary on the 99 Names
quiz.scholar_reflection: The Name Ar-Raqeeb means: the ever-watchful. Understanding the precise meaning allows you to call upon Allah by this Name at the right moment.

quiz.prompt: Which verse of the Quran affirms the Name Ar-Raqeeb for Allah?

options.text: Quran 4:1 — 'Indeed Allah is ever, over you, Ar-Raqeeb (an Observer)'
Quran 2:186 — 'And when My servants ask you concerning Me, indeed I am near'
Quran 6:103 — 'Vision perceives Him not, but He perceives all vision'
Quran 57:3 — 'He is the First and the Last, the Ascendant and the Intimate'

quiz.citation: Quran 4:1 — 'Indeed Allah is ever, over you, Ar-Raqeeb (an Observer).'
quiz.scholar_reflection: Allah affirms this Name for Himself: 'Indeed Allah is ever, over you, Ar-Raqeeb (an Observer).' (Quran 4:1). A Name is established for Allah only by the Quran or the authentic Sunnah — never by human invention.

quiz.prompt: What is the Arabic root that the Name Ar-Raqeeb is derived from?

options.text: Ra-qa-ba (ر ق ب) — to watch, to observe closely, to keep guard over
Ra-ka-ba (ر ك ب) — to mount or ride
Ra-gha-ba (ر غ ب) — to desire or wish for
Ra-qa-'a (ر ق ع) — to patch or mend

quiz.citation: Classical Arabic lexicography of the Divine Names — Ibn Uthaymeen, Commentary on the 99 Names
quiz.scholar_reflection: The Name comes from the root ra-qa-ba (ر ق ب), meaning to watch, to observe closely, to keep guard over. Ar-Raqeeb is the One whose watching never lapses — an observer who guards and preserves what He observes.

quiz.prompt: According to the hadith, how many Names of Allah are there, and what is promised to the one who enumerates them?

options.text: Ninety-nine — whoever enumerates them will enter Paradise
One hundred — whoever writes them will be forgiven
Ninety-nine — whoever recites them nightly will be granted wealth
Seventy — whoever memorises them will be raised in rank

quiz.scholar_reflection: The Prophet said: 'Verily to Allah belongs ninety-nine names, one hundred less one. Whoever enumerates them will enter paradise.' Scholars explain that enumerating (ihsa') means memorising them, understanding their meanings, worshipping Allah by them, and calling upon Him through them.

quiz.prompt: What does the Quran command believers to do with the Most Beautiful Names of Allah?

options.text: Call upon Him by them
Recite them only in Ramadan
Write them on the walls of the masjid
Keep them hidden from the general people

quiz.citation: Quran 7:180 — 'And to Allah belong the best Names, so call upon Him by them'
quiz.scholar_reflection: The Names were revealed to be used. Allah does not merely inform us of them — He commands us to call upon Him by them, which means matching the Name to the need in the moment of du'a.

quiz.prompt: Allah is Ar-Raqeeb — the ever-watchful. When in your life have you most needed Him to be this for you?
quiz.slider_label: How often do you call upon Allah by this specific Name?

options.text: In a moment of fear or danger
When I needed something no one else could provide
When I felt ashamed or broken
I have not thought about needing this quality specifically

quiz.scholar_reflection: The Names of Allah become real to us in the moments we need them most. Each Name is a door — Allah placed exactly this Name in your path at exactly this moment.

quiz.prompt: If you truly believed Allah is Ar-Raqeeb at every moment, what would change first in how you live?
quiz.slider_label: How much does this Name currently shape your daily choices?

options.text: How I speak when no one is listening
What I chase and what I let go of
How much anxiety I carry about the future
How I treat people who cannot benefit me

quiz.scholar_reflection: Ibn Uthaymeen taught that knowledge of a Name is incomplete until it changes conduct. The test of knowing a Name is not what you can recite about it, but what you do differently because of it.

quiz.prompt: Which obstacle most keeps you from living with awareness that Allah is Ar-Raqeeb?
quiz.slider_label: How present is this awareness in an ordinary day?

options.text: Distraction — I simply forget
Doubt — I know it intellectually but do not feel it
Habit — my routines were built without it
Impatience — I want to see it proven on my timeline

quiz.scholar_reflection: Naming the obstacle honestly is the beginning of removing it. The Quran repeatedly links forgetfulness of Allah to the corrosion of the heart — awareness is a practice, not a mood.

quiz.prompt: How would you explain the Name Ar-Raqeeb to someone who has never heard of it?
quiz.slider_label: How confident are you in your understanding of this Name?

options.text: Through a story from my own life
Through the verse of the Quran that affirms it
Through what it means about Allah's perfection
I could not yet explain it clearly

quiz.scholar_reflection: Being able to teach a Name simply is a sign you have understood it. If you cannot yet explain it, that is not failure — it marks exactly where your study should continue.

quiz.prompt: What du'a will you make tonight, calling on Allah specifically as Ar-Raqeeb?
quiz.slider_label: How specific are your du'as usually?

options.text: For something I have been afraid to ask for
For someone else who needs it more than me
For steadiness rather than for change
For forgiveness before anything else

quiz.citation: Quran 7:180 — 'And to Allah belong the best Names, so call upon Him by them'
quiz.scholar_reflection: This is the final step of ihsa' — moving the Name from the mind to the tongue in supplication. A du'a that names the attribute you are relying on is a du'a that knows who it is addressing.
